Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

## Objective
- Turn the existing Spanish horror game into a complete, playable 3D hotel-survival game and verify it in a browser.

## Requirements
- Preserve the hotel horror setting, survival-game feel, and Spanish interface.
- Build on the existing game, making reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- Check browser screenshots during development, save small JPEGs (viewport no wider than 1280px), and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js for the 3D scene.
- Include room progression, keys, survival meters, inventory, enemy, hiding, flashlight, desktop/mobile controls, and win/lose/restart flow.
- Treat the face as a horror effect revealed where the flashlight shines, based on the truncated original request.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `index.html` with the Spanish 3D-game interface and added local Three.js r160 at `vendor/three.min.js`.
- Implemented the game in `game.js`, including rooms, pickups, interactions, survival systems, enemy, flashlight/face effect, controls, and endings.
- Installed Chromium for Playwright, opened `http://localhost:3002`, started the game, and inspected the latest screenshot saved at `/tmp/opencode/hotel-latest.jpg`.
- Fixed room cleanup by tracking/removing `state.roomGroup`.
- Tightened interaction targeting so objects must be nearby and either close or in front of the player.

### Active
- Continue testing the core gameplay loop, including room progression, item pickup/use, enemy behavior, mobile controls, endings, and restart.
- Recheck browser console and capture/inspect a fresh small JPEG after further changes.

### Blocked
- The original request ended mid-sentence, so the exact intended face behavior remains uncertain.

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` and retest the game in Chromium.
2. Test progression through all rooms, keys, survival items, enemy, hiding, and win/lose/restart; check mobile controls.
3. Fix any issues, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, overlays, controls, and script loading.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene and gameplay implementation.
- `vendor/three.min.js`: Local Three.js runtime.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

- Changes are uncommitted: `index.html` is modified; `game.js` and `vendor/` are untracked.

## Objective
- Complete the Spanish 3D hotel-survival horror game and verify it in a browser.
- Update the first level and enemy behavior to match the requested survival mechanics.

## Requirements
- Preserve the hotel horror setting, survival-game feel, and Spanish interface.
- Make the flashlight brighter and add adjustable camera sensitivity.
- Make the first level an infected area with the key in a drawer, wardrobes against walls, and destructed furniture.
- Let the demon patrol from hallway to hallway rather than chase the player; a red alarm should warn of its approach.
- Allow hiding inside wardrobes or crouching under tables.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js for the 3D scene.
- Keep room progression, keys, survival meters, inventory, flashlight/face effect, desktop and mobile controls, and win/lose/restart flow.
- Keep the player facing north after room transitions.
- Add a camera-sensitivity slider under an AJUSTES control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the existing Spanish UI and Three.js gameplay, including rooms, pickups, interactions, survival meters, enemy, controls, and endings.
- Fixed room cleanup, interaction targeting, transition yaw, mobile touch camera look, pointer capture handling, and related earlier issues.
- Added an inline SVG favicon and removed `window.__hotelDebug`.
- Added settings-panel styling and markup, an AJUSTES button, a camera-sensitivity slider, and revised intro text describing the first-level and alarm mechanics.

### Active
- Implement the requested first-level layout and drawer-based key placement.
- Replace enemy pursuit with hallway patrol and a red approach alarm.
- Make wardrobes wall-adjacent hiding places and support crouching under tables.
- Increase flashlight range/brightness and wire the sensitivity control into desktop and touch camera input.
- Verify item pickup/use, hiding, enemy behavior, and updated visuals in-browser.

### Blocked
- Browser interaction tests for pickup/use, hiding, and enemy behavior were previously inconclusive; those mechanics still need controlled verification.
- The latest HTML edits have not yet been checked in a browser or validated alongside `game.js`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and update `game.js` for flashlight strength, sensitivity, drawer key, table hiding, and non-chasing patrol/alarm behavior.
2. Run `node --check game.js` and test the updated game at `http://localhost:3002/`.
3. Verify the alarm, hiding, key pickup/use, settings control, and restart; inspect a fresh screenshot if needed.
4. Check `git status` and report the resulting uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Spanish interface, responsive controls, new settings panel, and intro text.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, room layout, enemy logic, flashlight, interactions, and controls.
- `vendor/three.min.js`: Local Three.js r160 runtime.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `M index.html`, `?? game.js`, `?? vendor/`.
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Before the latest request, `node --check game.js` passed and the browser console had zero errors; restart was verified.
- Existing `game.js` still places the first room’s key at `(-4.9, 2.8)`, spawns the enemy at `(-3, -3)`, and moves it toward the player; the requested drawer and patrol behavior remain unimplemented.
- `playwright-cli run-code` failed repeatedly with `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'page'`; `playwright-cli eval` supports page expressions.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the Spanish 3D hotel-survival horror game and verify it in a browser.
- Update the first level and enemy behavior to match the requested survival mechanics.

## Requirements
- Preserve the hotel horror setting, survival-game feel, and Spanish interface.
- Make the flashlight brighter and add adjustable camera sensitivity.
- Make the first level an infected area with the key in a drawer, wardrobes against walls, and destructed furniture.
- Let the demon patrol rather than chase; use a red alarm to warn of its approach.
- Allow hiding inside wardrobes or crouching under tables.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js for the 3D scene.
- Keep room progression, keys, survival meters, inventory, flashlight/face effect, desktop and mobile controls, and win/lose/restart flow.
- Keep the player facing north after room transitions.
- Put the camera-sensitivity slider under an AJUSTES control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented first-room infected details, wall-adjacent wardrobes, broken furniture, and a key hidden until its drawer is opened.
- Replaced player-chasing enemy movement with waypoint patrol and added a red approach alarm with an audio warning.
- Added wardrobe and under-table hiding interactions.
- Increased flashlight intensity and range; wired camera sensitivity into mouse and touch look.
- Added AJUSTES panel, slider, and updated Spanish intro instructions.
- `node --check game.js` produced no errors; `http://localhost:3002/` returns HTTP 200.

### Active
- Verify the updated game in a browser, including drawer/key pickup, hiding, patrol/alarm, settings, and restart.

### Blocked
- Browser interaction tests have not yet been run; earlier interaction tests were inconclusive.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:3002/` in Playwright and check the console and updated visuals.
2. Test the drawer/key, wardrobe and table hiding, alarm and patrol behavior, sensitivity slider, and restart flow.
3. Review `git status` and report the uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Spanish interface, settings panel, and updated intro.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, first-room layout, interactions, enemy behavior, flashlight, and controls.
- `vendor/three.min.js`: Local Three.js runtime.

## Important Context
- Changes remain uncommitted: `M index.html`, `?? game.js`, `?? vendor/`.
- Game server is available at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- `playwright-cli run-code` previously failed with `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'page'`; `playwright-cli eval` supports page expressions.
